notes: Some points to remember of testcases
1. JBP = Job Board Plan — a commitment-tracking module (NOT financial). Admin creates/closes cycles; Channel Partners (CP) submit commitment forms in the CP Portal; admin reviews edit requests.
2. Admin master OTP = 258369; UAT admin mobile = 8888888888. Admin URL = https://uat-web.xrportal.in/admin/jbp-management.
3. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state (e.g. an OPEN cycle, a CP submission, a PENDING edit request, an editableUntil-expired request) must be supplied before executing this test.
4. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS or contradicted across docs; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

5. Destructive tests (Create Cycle / Close Cycle / Approve / Reject) mutate stateful UAT data and the single-OPEN-cycle constraint — require user authorisation before running on UAT (CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline #7).

6. Only ONE OPEN cycle is allowed at a time. Creating a cycle while one is OPEN raises an "Active Cycle Detected" popup. Closing a cycle is irreversible. Creating a new cycle cascade-CLOSES the previous OPEN cycle and EXPIRES its PENDING/APPROVED edit requests.

7. DOC_DRIFT (observed/FSD-corrected values win over BRD/FRD): (a) DOC_DRIFT-JBP-001 — APPROVE requires `editWindow` (hours, integer >=1); `adminComment` is OPTIONAL on approve, REQUIRED on reject (BRD/FRD "reason required on approve" is stale). (b) DOC_DRIFT-JBP-002 — edit-request statuses are Pending -> APPROVED/REJECTED -> EXPIRED (timeout) / CONSUMED (CP resubmit); submissions are ACTIVE/EXPIRED. (c) DOC_DRIFT-JBP-003 — NO CP notification is sent on admin approve/reject (BRD "CP receives notification" is stale); the ONLY JBP notification is the CP-submit WhatsApp template `jbplaunchtwo_new`. (d) DOC_DRIFT-JBP-005 — create-cycle modal submit button is labelled "Create Cycle" (per visual-memory), not "Submit". (e) DOC_DRIFT-JBP-006 — cycles have no PUT/DELETE route (return 404); Create-or-Close only.

8. Auto-sweep is triggered by the LIST GET calls themselves: GET /jbp-cycles auto-CLOSEs OPEN cycles whose endDate is past; GET /jbp-edit-requests auto-EXPIREs requests whose editableUntil is past. `editableUntil` on approve is clamped to the cycle endDate 23:59:59.999.

9. CP Portal side (form submission) is out of the Admin module's primary scope; CP-touching steps are flagged and use https://uat-web.xrportal.in/ login (CLAUDE.md), OTP 147258. Admin reviews the result via the Submissions tab.

10. Notifications glossary: WhatsApp dispatch is fire-and-forget (submission still succeeds if WhatsApp fails); LSQ createActivity (event 270) + captureLead (CustomObject 14-28) run BEFORE the DB write, so an LSQ 500 BLOCKS the whole submission. LSQ is excluded from credentialed automation (CLAUDE.md) — verify its availability effect manually / [VERIFY WITH DEV].

tcs.scenario: To verify the JBP Management page loads
tcs.description: Verify that the JBP Management page opens at /admin/jbp-management when an admin clicks the JBP menu item.
tcs.precond: An admin is logged in (mobile 8888888888 / OTP 258369).
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Admin portal.
2. Click "JBP Management" in the left sidebar.
3. Watch the URL and the page content load.
tcs.expected:
The browser lands on /admin/jbp-management. The page shows the "JBP Management" heading and three tabs. The page finishes loading within ~5 seconds.
Source: visual-memory jbp-full.png + BRD §3 + FRD §2.

tcs.scenario: To verify JBP page is protected without a session
tcs.description: Verify that opening /admin/jbp-management with no active admin session redirects to the login page.

Response contains only cycles within [d1,d2]. Note: this GET also auto-CLOSEs any OPEN cycle whose endDate is past (see ADM_JBP_FSD_044).

tcs.scenario: To verify the single-OPEN-cycle constraint at create

1. Click "+ Create Cycle".
2. Fill the form with a valid name and dates.
3. Submit.
tcs.expected:
An "Active Cycle Detected" popup is shown and the new cycle is NOT created. The existing OPEN cycle must be closed first.
Source: BRD §7.1 + FS Feat3 §6 rule 3.

Source: FRD §11 (POST) + dimension 8 (UI-vs-backend).

tcs.scenario: To verify the close-cycle API endpoint
tcs.description: Verify PUT /api/v1/admin/jbp-cycles/:id/close transitions an OPEN cycle to CLOSED and rejects an already-CLOSED cycle.
tcs.precond: Valid admin token; one OPEN and one CLOSED cycle id. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. PUT /jbp-cycles/<openId>/close.
2. PUT /jbp-cycles/<closedId>/close again.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin token; open + closed cycle ids
tcs.expected:
The OPEN cycle becomes CLOSED. Re-closing a CLOSED cycle is rejected. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact error/status for the second call.
Source: FRD §11 (PUT /close) + FSD §"Auto-Close Cascade".

tcs.scenario: To verify a CLOSED cycle cannot be reopened

tcs.scenario: To verify reopen cannot be forced via the API

tcs.steps: 1. Attempt any call intended to set a CLOSED cycle back to OPEN (e.g. PUT on the cycle).
tcs.expected:
No route reopens the cycle. Per ADM_JBP_FSD_048, PUT/DELETE on cycles return 404 — reopen is impossible by design.

tcs.scenario: [FSD-CORRECTION][DOC_DRIFT-JBP-006] No PUT or DELETE on cycles
tcs.description: Verify that admins cannot edit or delete a created cycle — there is no PUT or DELETE route for cycles; both return 404.
tcs.precond: A cycle exists. Valid admin token. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/admin/jbp-cycles/:id with new dates.
2. DELETE /api/v1/admin/jbp-cycles/:id.
tcs.expected:
Both calls return 404 (route not registered). Cycles can only be Created or Closed. Document as a known limitation (DOC_DRIFT-JBP-006 — docs implied editability).
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) + FRD §11.

tcs.scenario: To verify the submissions list API
tcs.description: Verify GET /api/v1/admin/jbp-submissions returns submissions filtered by cycleId/projectId.
tcs.precond: Valid admin token; a cycle with submissions. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].

tcs.expected:
Only ACTIVE submissions for that cycle are returned. Note each row's `updatedAt` is undefined (see ADM_JBP_FSD_051).

tcs.scenario: To verify EXPIRED edit requests appear and are not actionable
tcs.description: Verify that an APPROVED edit request whose editableUntil has passed is shown as EXPIRED after the list auto-sweep, and cannot be re-approved/re-rejected.
tcs.precond: At least one APPROVED edit request whose editableUntil is in the past. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Edit Requests tab (this GET triggers the auto-sweep).
2. Apply Status filter = EXPIRED.
3. Inspect the previously-APPROVED request and its available actions.

tcs.expected:
The previously-APPROVED request now shows status EXPIRED; admin cannot re-approve or re-reject it. (Auto-sweep on GET — see ADM_JBP_FSD_045.)
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) + DOC_DRIFT-JBP-002.

tcs.scenario: To verify pagination on the Edit Requests table
tcs.description: Verify that the Edit Requests table paginates when there is more than one page of requests.

tcs.steps: 1. Click the next-page control in the pager.
tcs.expected:
The next page of edit requests loads; any active filter is preserved.
Source: dimension 11 + FS Feat6.

tcs.description: Verify that when there are no edit requests the tab shows an empty state, not an error.

Empty state / zero rows with no error. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact empty-state text.

tcs.scenario: To verify opening an EXPIRED/CONSUMED request hides actions
tcs.description: Verify that opening an EXPIRED or CONSUMED edit request shows it read-only with no approve/reject actions.

tcs.expected:
The request is read-only; no Approve/Reject controls are offered. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact UI treatment.

tcs.scenario: To verify the edit-requests list API and its auto-sweep
tcs.description: Verify GET /api/v1/admin/jbp-edit-requests returns requests and triggers the EXPIRE auto-sweep.
tcs.precond: Valid admin token; a PENDING/APPROVED request with editableUntil in the past. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Confirm the request status in DB.
2. Call GET /api/v1/admin/jbp-edit-requests.
3. Re-check the request status.
tcs.expected:
The list returns the requests; the expired request's status is now EXPIRED after the GET (auto-sweep). See ADM_JBP_FSD_045.
Source: FRD §11 + FSD-CORRECTION.

tcs.scenario: [FSD-CORRECTION][DOC_DRIFT-JBP-001/003] Approve sets editableUntil, does NOT update submission, sends NO CP notification
tcs.description: Verify that approving an edit request requires editWindow (hours), sets editableUntil and reviewer fields, does NOT immediately update the submission, and dispatches NO notification to the CP.
tcs.precond: A Pending edit request detail is open. Valid admin. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED]. User authorisation to mutate UAT.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Approve.
2. Enter editWindow = 24 (hours); optional adminComment.
3. Submit.
4. Check the CP's phone/email/WhatsApp for any notification.
5. Inspect the original JbpSubmission row — is it changed?
tcs.expected:
Edit request status -> APPROVED; editableUntil = now + 24h (clamped to cycle endDate 23:59:59.999); reviewedBy = admin.id, reviewedAt = now. The ORIGINAL submission is NOT updated yet — it changes only when the CP resubmits (then old row -> EXPIRED, new ACTIVE row version+1). NO notification is dispatched to the CP (DOC_DRIFT-JBP-003 — verified by source).
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) + FS Feat6 §7/§8.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Approve dialog fields
tcs.description: Verify the Approve action presents an editWindow input (hours) and an optional adminComment field.
tcs.precond: A Pending edit request detail is open; Approve clicked.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Approve.
2. Read the input fields offered.
tcs.expected:
An editWindow field (hours, integer >=1, required) and an adminComment field (optional, max 550 chars) are shown. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact on-screen labels — FSD names the payload fields; visual-memory did not capture the approve dialog.
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) + DOC_DRIFT-JBP-001.

tcs.scenario: [FSD-CORRECTION][DOC_DRIFT-JBP-001] Approve requires editWindow, not a reason
tcs.description: Verify that approving without editWindow is rejected with a validation error, and that adminComment is optional.
tcs.precond: A Pending edit request detail is open; Approve clicked.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Approve.
2. Submit without entering editWindow.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a Pending edit request; editWindow omitted
tcs.expected:
Validation error on editWindow — required integer min 1. adminComment is OPTIONAL (nullable, max 550 chars). The prior BRD/FRD claim "reason required for approve" is WRONG (DOC_DRIFT-JBP-001).
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook).

tcs.scenario: To verify editWindow numeric boundaries
tcs.description: Verify editWindow rejects 0, negative, and decimal values and accepts the minimum integer 1.
tcs.precond: A Pending edit request; Approve clicked.
tcs.steps:
1. Try editWindow = 0 -> submit.
2. Try editWindow = -5 -> submit.
3. Try editWindow = 2.5 -> submit.
4. Try editWindow = 1 -> submit.
tcs.expected:
0, negative, and decimal are rejected (required integer min 1); editWindow = 1 is accepted. [VERIFY WITH DEV] documented upper bound (if any).
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (integer min 1) + dimension 3 (boundary).

tcs.scenario: [BUG-REF: BUG-JBP-002] editableUntil is clamped to cycle endDate
tcs.description: Verify that approving with an editWindow longer than the time remaining in the cycle clamps editableUntil to the cycle endDate, not now+editWindow.
tcs.precond: A cycle whose endDate is 3 days away; a Pending edit request on a submission in that cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Approve with editWindow = 240 (10 days).
2. Inspect editableUntil in the DB or the CP "latest cycle" view.
tcs.expected:
editableUntil = cycle endDate 23:59:59.999 (NOT now + 240h). The cycle endDate caps the window.
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) BUG-JBP-002.

tcs.scenario: To verify approving an already-EXPIRED request is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that if a request auto-EXPIRES (via the list sweep) before approve is confirmed, the approve is rejected.
tcs.precond: A request whose editableUntil/state causes it to be swept to EXPIRED between opening and confirming. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Open Approve on a request.
2. Trigger the auto-sweep (e.g. reload list) so the request becomes EXPIRED.
3. Confirm the approve.
tcs.expected:
[VERIFY WITH DEV] The approve should be rejected because the request is no longer PENDING. Document the actual response.
Source: DOC_DRIFT-JBP-002 + dimension 4 (race).

tcs.scenario: To verify approve is blocked on a non-Pending request

tcs.steps: 1. Attempt to approve a non-Pending request (via UI if shown, or API).
tcs.expected:
Approve is blocked / not offered for non-Pending requests. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact error.

tcs.scenario: To verify the approve API endpoint body
tcs.description: Verify PUT /api/v1/admin/jbp-edit-requests/:id/approve enforces editWindow and accepts optional adminComment.

tcs.scenario: [FSD-CORRECTION] CP resubmit consumes APPROVED edit request -> CONSUMED
tcs.description: Verify that when a CP resubmits within editableUntil, the old submission is EXPIRED, a new ACTIVE submission (version+1) is inserted, and the APPROVED edit request becomes CONSUMED.
tcs.precond: A CP has an APPROVED edit request still within editableUntil and an existing ACTIVE submission for the cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].

1. CP POST /api/v1/cp/jbp with new values.
2. Inspect the DB rows for that CP+cycle.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CP token; APPROVED request within editableUntil; CP Portal [VERIFY WITH DEV] URL — DOC_DRIFT-JBP-004
tcs.expected:
Old JbpSubmission -> EXPIRED. New JbpSubmission inserted with version = previous.version + 1, status ACTIVE. The APPROVED edit-request row -> CONSUMED.
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) + DOC_DRIFT-JBP-002.

tcs.scenario: [FSD-CORRECTION][DOC_DRIFT-JBP-003] Reject preserves original submission, sends NO CP notification
tcs.description: Verify that rejecting an edit request with an adminComment sets the request to REJECTED, preserves the original submission, and dispatches NO CP notification.

tcs.description: Verify PUT /api/v1/admin/jbp-edit-requests/:id/reject requires adminComment and preserves the original submission.

After the GET, the row's status is EXPIRED. The auto-sweep is triggered by the list call itself.

tcs.scenario: To verify closing a cycle sends NO CP notification (silent by design)
tcs.description: Verify that closing a JBP cycle dispatches no notification to CPs.
tcs.precond: An OPEN cycle exists. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED]. User authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Close the OPEN cycle (confirm "Yes, Close").
2. Check for any CP SMS/WhatsApp/email tied to the close.
tcs.expected:
No CP notification is dispatched on cycle close (silence-by-design). Only the success toast is shown.
Source: FS Feat4 §8 (None — no CP notification on close).

tcs.scenario: To verify CP submit fires the WhatsApp template (the ONLY JBP notification)
tcs.description: Verify that a successful CP JBP submission dispatches the WhatsApp template jbplaunchtwo_new — the only notification in the whole JBP flow.
tcs.precond: An OPEN cycle exists; a CP submits successfully. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CP submission.
tcs.steps:
1. CP submits a JBP form successfully.
2. Capture the outbound notification channel and template name.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP submission; CP Portal [VERIFY WITH DEV] URL — DOC_DRIFT-JBP-004
tcs.expected:
A WhatsApp message using template jbplaunchtwo_new is dispatched. No admin-side action (create/close/approve/reject) sends any notification (DOC_DRIFT-JBP-003).
Source: FS Feat6 §8 (FSD-CORRECTION) + ADM_JBP_FSD_041.

tcs.scenario: [BUG-REF: BUG-JBP-001] WhatsApp template ${+91} emits "91" (template-string bug)
tcs.description: Verify the phone-number placeholder in the jbplaunchtwo_new WhatsApp dispatch resolves to "91<phone>" (missing the literal +) due to a JS template-literal bug.
tcs.precond: A CP submits a JBP successfully. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Capture the WhatsApp dispatch payload to template jbplaunchtwo_new.
2. Inspect the phone-number placeholder.
tcs.expected:
The placeholder containing ${+91}<phone> resolves to "91<phone>" — missing the literal + sign (JS evaluates +91 as numeric 91). Document as a template bug.
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) BUG-JBP-001.

tcs.scenario: [FSD-CORRECTION] CP submit WhatsApp is fire-and-forget
tcs.description: Verify that a WhatsApp dispatch failure does not fail the CP submission — the DB row is still created and the CP sees success.
tcs.precond: Backend outbound to botspice WhatsApp is blocked/failing. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. CP submits a JBP.
2. Verify a new ACTIVE submission row exists in the DB.
3. Verify no error is returned to the CP.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] blocked WhatsApp outbound; a CP submission
tcs.expected:
The DB row is created and the CP sees a success response; the WhatsApp call fails silently in the background. Audit log captures success regardless.
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook).

tcs.scenario: [FSD-CORRECTION] LSQ outage blocks the entire JBP submission
tcs.description: Verify that an LSQ failure (called before the DB write) blocks the whole CP submission with HTTP 500 and no DB row.
tcs.precond: LSQ is mocked/forced to return 500. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED]. LSQ is excluded from credentialed automation (CLAUDE.md) — verify the availability effect manually.
tcs.steps:
1. CP attempts submitJbp while LSQ returns 500.
2. Observe the HTTP response and the DB state.
tcs.expected:
LSQ createActivity (event 270) AND captureLead (CustomObject 14-28) are called BEFORE the DB write. If either fails -> HTTP 500 to the CP and NO DB row is inserted. Document as an availability risk. [VERIFY WITH DEV] (LSQ excluded from automation).
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) + CLAUDE.md LSQ exclusion.

tcs.scenario: To verify the OPEN cycle appears as the active cycle in the CP banner
tcs.description: Verify that the cycle currently OPEN in the Admin Cycle Management tab is the one shown as the active cycle in the CP Portal JBP banner.
tcs.precond: Exactly one OPEN cycle exists. CP login available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Note the OPEN cycle name in the Admin Cycle Management tab.
2. Log into the CP Portal and open JBP.
3. Read the "Current Cycle - <name>" banner.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] one OPEN cycle; CP login (8888888888 / 147258); CP Portal [VERIFY WITH DEV] URL — DOC_DRIFT-JBP-004
tcs.expected:
The CP banner shows "Current Cycle - <name>" with an ACTIVE badge and "Closes on: <End Date>" matching the OPEN admin cycle.
Source: FRD §3 (CP Portal banner) + FS Feat7 §4. CP-side — flagged, verify cross-module reflection.

tcs.scenario: To verify a closed cycle disappears from the CP active banner
tcs.description: Verify that after an admin closes the OPEN cycle, the CP Portal no longer shows it as active and the "Add New JBP Entry" button disappears.
tcs.precond: One OPEN cycle exists; a CP has not yet submitted. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED]. User authorisation to close.
tcs.steps:
1. Close the OPEN cycle in the Admin tab.
2. Refresh the CP Portal JBP page.
3. Look for the active banner and the Add New JBP Entry button.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] one OPEN cycle; CP login; CP Portal [VERIFY WITH DEV] URL
tcs.expected:
After the close, the CP Portal stops showing the cycle as active and the "Add New JBP Entry" button disappears.
Source: FS Feat4 §7 (CP Portal stops showing active) + FS Feat7 §6.

tcs.scenario: To verify an invalid/expired token is rejected (401/403)
tcs.description: Verify that JBP admin API calls with an invalid or expired bearer token are rejected with 401/403.
tcs.precond: An invalid or expired admin token. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/admin/jbp-cycles with an invalid/expired token.
2. Observe the response status.
tcs.expected:
The call is rejected with 401 (or 403); no cycle data is returned. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact status code.
Source: FRD §3 (admin session required) + dimension 9.
Note: per Login-master notes, logout is a server-side no-op (JWT stays valid ~1 day) — do not treat post-logout calls as 401.

tcs.scenario: To verify JBP data is isolated per project/tenant
tcs.description: Verify that an admin scoped to one project cannot see another project's JBP cycles/submissions.
tcs.precond: Cycles/submissions exist under at least two projects. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. As an admin for project A, list cycles and submissions.
2. Confirm no project-B records appear.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] JBP data under two projects; admin scoped to project A
tcs.expected:
Only the current project's JBP cycles/submissions are returned (projectId scoping). [VERIFY WITH DEV] multi-tenant scoping — not detailed in BRD/FRD.
Source: FRD §10 (projectId FK) + dimension 9 (data isolation).

tcs.scenario: To verify approve/reject require an admin token
tcs.description: Verify that the approve and reject endpoints reject calls without a valid admin token.
tcs.precond: A Pending edit request id. No / non-admin token. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. PUT /jbp-edit-requests/:id/approve with no token.
2. PUT /jbp-edit-requests/:id/reject with no token.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] pending request id; no admin token
tcs.expected:
Both calls are rejected (401/403); no status change occurs. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact status.
Source: FRD §3 + §11 + dimension 9.

tcs.scenario: [BUG-REF: BUG-JBP-003] submitJbp NPE on null cycle
tcs.description: Verify that submitting with a jbpCycleId not present in the DB throws a TypeError (jbpCycle.endDate read before the null check) instead of a clean 400.
tcs.precond: A CP supplies an invalid jbpCycleId. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/cp/jbp with jbpCycleId = 999999 (not in DB).
2. Observe the response.
tcs.expected:
The backend throws a TypeError on jbpCycle.endDate instead of returning HTTP 400 "Cycle not found". Document as a bug (BUG-JBP-003).
Source: FSD-CORRECTION (workbook) BUG-JBP-003.

tcs.scenario: To verify a server 500 on the cycle list is handled gracefully
tcs.description: Verify that if the cycle-list call returns a 500, the JBP page shows an error state rather than a blank/broken page.
tcs.precond: The cycle-list endpoint is forced to 500. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Force GET /api/v1/admin/jbp-cycles to 500.
2. Open the Cycle Management tab.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a forced 500 on the list endpoint
tcs.expected:
The page shows an error message / retry affordance and does not crash. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact error text.
Source: dimension 5 (server 500).

tcs.scenario: To verify a network drop mid-create is handled
tcs.description: Verify that losing connectivity while submitting Create Cycle surfaces an error and does not create a duplicate/partial cycle.
tcs.precond: The Create New Cycle modal is open with valid data; no OPEN cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED].
tcs.steps:
1. Fill the create form.
2. Drop the network just as Create Cycle is clicked.
3. Restore the network and reload the list.
tcs.expected:
An error is surfaced; no duplicate or partial cycle is created. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact behaviour and any retry.
Source: dimension 5 (network failure).

tcs.scenario: To verify a very long cycle name is handled
tcs.description: Verify the Cycle Name field handles an extremely long value (boundary) without breaking layout or the create call.
tcs.precond: The Create New Cycle modal is open; no OPEN cycle.
tcs.steps:
1. Enter a 256+ character Cycle Name.
2. Set valid dates and submit.
tcs.expected:
[VERIFY WITH DEV] The field either enforces a max length or accepts and stores/truncates it without breaking layout. Document the max length.
Source: dimension 11 (input boundary) — no documented max in BRD/FRD/FS.
